keyTerms.definition: P06, P07, P10, with local remediation R55-R57.
Trees, impurity, splits, pruning, bagging, forests, boosting, imbalance, importance, baselines.

recall.question: What must a learner do after this lesson?
recall.answer: Score a split with Gini, prune with a cost penalty, run AdaBoost and one gradient-boost step by hand, derive the variance formula, beat a baseline.

keyTerms.definition: Labeled as such throughout.
Russian-doll ladder positions 0-10 marking each step.

recall.question: What does computed 2026-10-06 mark?
recall.answer: Numbers from compute_completion.py, numpy 1.26.4, seed 7.

keyTerms.definition: A fenced rectangle voting the majority label inside it.
Prediction is a walk down the fences, then a lookup.

recall.question: What does the C01 tree predict at (0.9, 0.1)?
recall.answer: 1: x1 > 0.5, x2 <= 0.5, the lower-right rectangle votes 1.

recall.question: What did the noisy point cost?
recall.answer: Train accuracy 5/6: the upper-right rectangle absorbed the label noise.

keyTerms.definition: 1 - sum p_k^2: the lazy-rule error rate.
-sum p_k log p_k: punishes near-ties harder than Gini.

recall.question: Score node [4,1].
recall.answer: Gini 0.32, entropy 0.5004, misclassification 0.2.

recall.question: Why is misclassification flat for growth?
recall.answer: It sees only the majority class: many splits tie at the same gain.

keyTerms.definition: Parent impurity minus weighted child impurity.
Sort once, sweep midpoints, track running counts: O(1) per candidate.

recall.question: Which threshold wins the C03 toy?
recall.answer: t = 0.5, gain 0.5, both children pure.

recall.question: Why does greedy fail on XOR?
recall.answer: Every single split scores gain 0; the pair would score perfectly.

keyTerms.definition: R(T) + alpha |T|: the exchange rate between error and leaves.
Grow the full tree, then collapse the weakest splits under the alpha budget.

recall.question: What did alpha 0.05 vs 0.1 decide?
recall.answer: 0.05: depth-2 wins (0.2 vs 0.225). 0.1: prune back to depth-1 (0.325 vs 0.4).

recall.question: Why does pruning beat early stopping?
recall.answer: A weak early split can enable a strong later one: the XOR lesson.

keyTerms.definition: n draws with replacement: some points double, some never appear.
(1-1/n)^n -> 36.8% in the large-n limit.

recall.question: Why does bagging not fix bias?
recall.answer: An XOR stump errs at 0.5 forever: bagging averages variance, not bias.

recall.question: What are the C07 out-of-bag sets?
recall.answer: Points missed by a replicate: point 0 misses rep 0, point 3 misses none.

keyTerms.definition: rho sigma^2 + (1-rho) sigma^2/B: the shared wobble no averaging removes.
Past it, extra trees buy almost nothing.

recall.question: What do rho=0.3, B=10 give?
recall.answer: 0.37 against the single-model 1.0.

recall.question: Why is the f04 curve not monotone?
recall.answer: B=25 scores worse than B=5 on six validation points: noise past the rho floor.

keyTerms.definition: Look at only mtry random features per split: decorrelates the trees.
Out-of-bag prediction: vote the trees whose replicate missed the point.

recall.question: What did the forest do to rho?
When is OOB optimistic?
recall.answer: Duplicates leak across the in-bag/OOB boundary: near-copy rows memorize the twin.

keyTerms.definition: 0.5 ln((1-eps)/eps): the stump's vote weight.
Missed points get heavier: the missed point holds half the weight after round 1.

recall.question: What were the round-1 numbers?
recall.answer: eps 0.25, alpha 0.5493, normalized weights [1/6,1/6,1/6,1/2].

recall.question: What does boosting do about label noise?
recall.answer: Nothing: round 2 spends half its attention on the noise point.

keyTerms.definition: r_i = y_i - F(x_i): the leftover error each round fits.
nu in (0,1]: small nu, more rounds, less memorization.

recall.question: What did one gradient-boost round do?
recall.answer: SSE 2.0 -> 0.5 on the three-point toy.

recall.question: How does gradient boosting generalize AdaBoost?
recall.answer: Fit the negative gradient of any loss; residuals for squared loss.

keyTerms.definition: Always-negative scores 0.95 and finds zero positives.
2PR/(P+R): 0.5714 on the toy from precision 0.4444, recall 0.8.

recall.question: Why can ROC-AUC look healthy while precision is poor?
recall.answer: True negatives dominate the false-positive rate on skewed data: read the PR curve.

recall.question: What is the fix order?
recall.answer: Class weights first, threshold moves second, resampling last.

keyTerms.definition: Sums impurity gain per feature: a property of the fitted tree, not the world.
Feature order, not physics: x1 and x2 correlate 1.0 here.

recall.question: What do the two importance columns disagree on?
recall.answer: Gain: x1 0.5, x2 0.0. Permutation: both perfect. The tree never reads x2.

recall.question: Why is importance not a deletion license?
recall.answer: The sensor was the cheap redundant backup; dropping it removed the only spare.

keyTerms.definition: The C03 stump: a smart baseline for nonlinear contenders.
A dumb reference next to every score: majority, stratified random, one-rule.

recall.question: What are the three rungs on the C03 toy?
recall.answer: Majority 0.5, stratified random 0.5, stump 1.0.

recall.question: What does a tie with the baseline mean?
recall.answer: Complexity without a beat is decoration: ship the baseline.

keyTerms.definition: An original PNG, opened and read on 2026-10-06.
Weight bars before and after round 1: the missed point at one half.

recall.question: What does f04 carry?
recall.answer: Bagged-stump validation MSE across B: the non-monotone curve and the single-stump line at 0.0421.

recall.answer: Its exact finite-sample distribution.
